cohort: The study included 200 pregnant women attending the antenatal clinic of Obstetrics and Gynaecology department of PGIMS Rohtak, India, who were randomly divided into an exercise group and a control group.
finding: A structured antenatal exercise program reduced the need for labor induction, shortened labor duration, increased the incidence of vaginal deliveries, and decreased pain perception during labor and delivery.
mod_finding: Antenatal exercise significantly increased the rate of vaginal deliveries (71% vs 56%) and decreased assisted vaginal deliveries (7% vs 20%), while cesarean section rates were comparable between the groups.
